subject.title: Rename i18n locale codes from region-based (zh-CN/zh-TW) to script-based (zh-Hans/zh-Hant)

question: Should OpenClaw make `zh-Hans` and `zh-Hant` the canonical Chinese locale IDs, and if so what migration or alias window should protect existing `zh-CN`/`zh-TW` users?
rationale: The requested rename is technically clear but changes shipped user-facing IDs, saved browser settings, CLI environment selection, generated file names, and docs tooling, so automation should not choose the compatibility policy.

options.title: Adopt script IDs with migration
options.body: Make `zh-Hans` and `zh-Hant` canonical and add a focused migration or deprecation path for existing `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` settings and environment inputs.

options.title: Keep current IDs
options.body: Leave `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` canonical to avoid churn and document that region IDs currently represent the maintained Simplified and Traditional bundles.

options.title: Split docs metadata from runtime IDs
options.body: Limit script-based naming to docs or publishing metadata while keeping runtime and CLI locale IDs unchanged.

recommendation.title: Adopt script IDs with migration
recommendation.body: Make `zh-Hans` and `zh-Hant` canonical and add a focused migration or deprecation path for existing `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` settings and environment inputs.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses CLI setup, docs, generated i18n, and compatibility policy, and steipete is the strongest routing owner from current blame and merged wizard i18n history.
